subject: Literature
title: Chinese Pangu and Cosmic Egg Myths
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Chinese Pangu and Cosmic Egg Myths.

hook.text: In Chinese mythology, the giant Pangu slept inside a cosmic egg for eighteen thousand years before waking.

buildup.text: When Pangu hatched, he separated chaos into sky and earth by pushing them apart with his growing body.

discovery.text: When he died, his body became the world: his breath became wind, his blood rivers, his hair the forests.

twist.text: The cosmic egg motif appears independently in Finnish, Indian, and African mythologies across the globe.

climax.text: These parallel creation myths suggest humans everywhere share deep narrative instincts about how worlds begin.

punchline.text: Cultures that never met imagined the same cosmic egg.

quiz.question: What is notable about the cosmic egg creation motif?
options: It only appears in Chinese mythology
It appears independently in multiple unconnected cultures worldwide
It was invented by modern scholars
